chunks: From him, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah, who said:
He said to him: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: Indeed, a man from the Ansar married while he was in the state of Ihram, so the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) annulled his marriage.

key_terms.الْأَنْصَارِ: The Ansar, the helpers of the Prophet from Medina
key_terms.رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ص: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him)
key_terms.مُحْرِمٌ: One in the state of Ihram, a ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah

ai.seo_question: Is a marriage valid if a man marries while in the state of Ihram for Hajj?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Isfahar establishes the invalidity (batl) of marriage contracted during Ihram, a ruling derived from the Prophet's annulment of an Ansari man's union. In Shia jurisprudence, this serves as a primary evidence for the prohibition of marriage for both men and women in the state of ritual consecration, linking marital eligibility directly to the spiritual purity required for Hajj and Umrah.
